bug_description.original: A crash occurs in Parser::makeStream when handling malformed files.
bug_description.normalized: A crash occurs in Parser::makeStream when handling malformed files.

source.description: Poppler project code consumes the attacker-controlled raw PDF buffer and creates a document parser object.

sink.description: Parser::makeStream calls setFlag on a stale XRefEntry pointer after xref reconstruction has freed/reallocated the entries array.

root_cause.description: makeStream caches an XRefEntry pointer before dictLookup, but dictLookup can reconstruct the xref table and invalidate that pointer.

tainted_value_origin.description: The stream dictionary Length lookup is the first vulnerability-relevant parse operation that can trigger xref reconstruction while entry is cached.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The attacker-controlled PDF is loaded by Poppler and reaches Parser::makeStream. makeStream caches an XRefEntry pointer in entry before parsing the stream Length. For malformed input, dict.dictLookup("Length") can fetch another object and trigger xref reconstruction, freeing/reallocating the entries array that owns the cached XRefEntry. The vulnerable code then continues to use the stale entry pointer at the end of makeStream and calls entry->setFlag, which dereferences freed memory in XRefEntry::setFlag.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch refreshes entry with xref->getEntry(objNum, false) after dictLookup, because dictLookup can reconstruct the xref table. The final entry->setFlag therefore uses a current XRefEntry pointer instead of the stale one, and the same PoC no longer crashes in the fixed build.
